newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish agri-food trade up 23 pct in 96-think-tanks.
newsitem.headline: Polish agri-food trade up 23 pct in 96-think-tanks.

text.p: Poland's bilateral trade in food and agricultural products grew by nearly 23 percent to $6.75 billion in 1996 over the previous year, according to an annual report by two agriculture ministry-linked think-tanks.

The report, by the Agricultural Policy Analysis Unit (SAEPR) and the Foreign Agricultural Markets Monitoring Unit (FAMMU), said Poland exported $2.76 billion worth of agri-food products last year, up from $2.51 billion in 1995, while running a deficit of $1.23 billion, up from $480 million.
Poland's leading exports were processed goods from fruit, confectionary products, processed meat and dairy products.
The main imports were grains, which accounted for nearly $740 million, coffee, cocoa and tea, reaching $460 million, and fresh fruit, at $300 million, the report said.
The European Union accounted for 47 percent of Polish agri-food exports, down from 55 percent in 1995, and 47 percent of imports, down from 49 percent.
Poland's food trade gap with EU countries ballooned to nearly $570 million in 1996 from $90 million.
Trade with former Soviet republics was most dynamic, with exports growing by 34 percent to $1.066 billion and imports by 55 percent to $170 million.
Agri-food trade makes up about 11 percent of Poland's total trade. --Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
